en: Let's talk about this POC piece because I think this is something a lot of people deal with.

en: And then I want to talk about this two-by-two that you have in the book.

en: And I'll actually pull it up.

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's talk about POCs first.

speaker: Unknown
en: So POCs, when we talk about POCs, many founders think about a POC as a proof of technical functionality, and is their product actually working in their customer environments.
zh: 所以 POC，当我们谈论 POC 时，许多创始人把 POC 看作是技术功能的证明，以及他们的产品是否真的在客户环境中工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they set up the expectation that we are saying, "Hey, we are going to put the product, and we're going to see if it actually works."
zh: 他们设立了这样的预期，我们在说，“嘿，我们要把产品放进去，我们要看看它是否真的工作。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And they would probably say, "Should I charge for a POC versus not?"
zh: 他们大概会说，“我应该对 POC 收费还是不收费？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And we'll unpack that in a bit, should you or should you not.
zh: 我们稍后会详细拆解这个问题，你应该还是不应该。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's actually a completely wrong way of framing it.
zh: 而这实际上是一个完全错误的框架设定。

speaker: Unknown
en: The POC should be framed as the entire goal of the POC is to create a business case, period, full stop.
zh: POC 应该被设定为，POC 的整个目标就是创建一个商业案例，句号，就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not to demonstrate product functionality fit within your customer environment's ability to integrate.
zh: 它不是为了演示产品功能是否适应客户环境的集成能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of that stuff is a consequence of the business case.
zh: 所有这些东西都是商业案例的附属结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you frame it this way is you can say, "Look, it is a 30-day pilot for co-creating an ROI model and building a business case along with their users.
zh: 所以如果你这样设定框架，你可以说，“看，这是一个 30 天的试点，用于共同创建一个 ROI 模型并与他们的用户一起构建商业案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we see value at the end of the 30 days based on the business case, we can get to commercial discussions."
zh: 如果我们在 30 天结束时根据商业案例看到了价值，我们可以进入商业讨论。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So that way you've actually not talked about your price.
zh: 这样一来，你实际上还没有谈论你的价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're only focused on co-creating a business case with the customer.
zh: 你只专注于与客户共创商业案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: And based on the business case, you can actually come up with a proper commercial agreement.
zh: 基于商业案例，你实际上可以提出一个恰当的商业协议。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if they see value, they're going to pay you for it.
zh: 如果他们看到了价值，他们就会为此付费。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thinking about the POCs in that kind of manner.
zh: 所以以这种方式来考虑 POC。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the question that I often get asked is, "Should I charge for a POC?"
zh: 我经常被问到的一个问题是，“我应该对 POC 收费吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And the answer is yes, but smartly.
zh: 答案是肯定的，但要聪明地收费。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's talk about why it's important to charge.
zh: 让我们谈谈为什么收费很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason you need to charge for a POC is you start isolating people who are just tire kickers versus serious buyers.
zh: 你需要对 POC 收费的原因是，你开始将那些只是随便看看的人与真正的买家区分开来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It becomes a lead qualification mechanism.
zh: 它成为一个线索筛选机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you didn't have that, you're going to attract all of these curious buyers who are just curious about AI.
zh: 如果没有那个，你会吸引所有这些好奇的买家，他们只是对 AI 感到好奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just want to see if it works or not.
zh: 他们只是想看看它是否有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will say, "Yes, I'll engage with the POC."
zh: 他们会说，“是的，我会参与这个 POC。”

speaker: Unknown
en: They will take 30, 60, 90 days with you.
zh: 他们会花费 30、60、90 天与你在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will burn a lot of resources, never buy.
zh: 他们会消耗大量资源，却从不购买。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've just wasted your time.
zh: 你刚刚浪费了你的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Time is of the essence.
zh: 时间至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So having a price tag to your POC actually indicates that there is seriousness on both sides, so you should charge.
zh: 所以给你的 POC 贴上价格标签实际上表明双方都有诚意，所以你应该收费。

speaker: Unknown
en: But how do you actually charge for it?
zh: 但你实际上如何收费呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to charge for it smartly.
zh: 你需要聪明地对它收费。

speaker: Unknown
en: What this means is that you need to make sure that your POC pricing is not a reflection of your actual commercial deal.
zh: 这意味着你需要确保你的 POC 定价并不反映你实际的商业交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because let's say if you just say it's a 10K POC for a 30-day pilot.
zh: 因为假设如果你只是说这是一个为期 30 天的试点 1 万美元的 POC。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't talk about the fact that it is not the same as your commercial discussion, you have now set an anchor that, okay, it's 120K per year kind of deal if the POC works.
zh: 如果你不讨论这与你的商业谈判不同这一事实，你现在就设定了一个锚点，好吧，如果 POC 有效，那就是每年 12 万美元的那种交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have to be clear that the 10K is only for building a business case.
zh: 所以你必须清楚说明这 1 万美元仅用于构建商业案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Commercial discussions will follow after that.
zh: 商业谈判将在那之后进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not an indication of the actual commercial discussion.
zh: 它不是实际商业谈判的指示。

speaker: Unknown
en: But your buyer on the other side might still push you saying, "That's all great, but I need a price or a budget, otherwise I won't move forward with it."
zh: 但另一边的买家可能仍然会推动你，说，“那都很棒，但我需要一个价格或预算，否则我不会继续推进。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are two ways to actually deflect those kind of questions.
zh: 所以有两种方法可以实际回避这类问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first way is contextualize the price on the value.
zh: 第一种方法是根据价值来设定价格背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can say something like, if you're pushed for price, "Hey, for customers such as yours, we have been able to at least unlock 10 million in very similar situations.
zh: 所以你可以这样说，如果被要求报价，“嘿，对于像你这样的客户，我们在非常类似的情况下至少解锁了 1000 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our pricing is... One is to 10X when it comes to ROI."
zh: 而我们的定价是……一个是 ROI 的 10 倍。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So you basically said that you're a million dollars to actually get started, but you actually didn't say it.
zh: 所以你基本上说的是你需要 100 万美元才能开始，但你实际上并没有明说。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just said, "It's a 10 million, and I'm taking one in 10 in exchange for it."
zh: 你只是说，“这是 1000 万，我从中抽取十分之一作为回报。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've given the buyer an indication, but you've framed it in such a manner that actually is justifiable, right?
zh: 所以你给了买家一个指示，但你用一种实际上是合理的方式来构建它，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: A one in 10X ROI.
zh: 一个 10 倍的 ROI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one way to do it.
zh: 这是其中一种方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: They might still say, "Yeah, that's good, but I need a budget."
zh: 他们可能仍然会说，“是的，那很好，但我需要一个预算。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So then rather than just give them a budget saying, "It could be a 200K option," don't do that.
zh: 所以不要只是给他们一个预算说，“这可能是 20 万美元的选项，”不要那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the worst thing you can actually say.
zh: 那是你能说的最糟糕的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Give them a range.
zh: 给他们一个范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can say something like, "Look, the final pricing would be anywhere from 500K to a million.
zh: 你可以说这样的话，“看，最终定价会在 50 万到 100 万之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And based on the business case that we would co-create with you, we can pick a point in that range that justifies the value that we bring to the table."
zh: 基于我们要与你共创的商业案例，我们可以在这个范围内选择一个点，证明我们带来的价值是合理的。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're giving budgetary ranges, right?
zh: 所以你是在给出预算范围，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the other way to actually go about POCs.
zh: 所以这是处理 POC 的另一种方式。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And picking those early wins is very, very critical.

speaker: Unknown
en: And having buyers who are serious, lead qualifying, having the right POC process, and thinking about POCs as, frankly, not just trying to see if your product actually works and delivers value, but it's a great chance to have a commercial test-and-learn experiment and have fun with it and try to see what you can bring to the table in terms of your value and what portion can you actually take.
zh: 拥有认真的买家，筛选线索，拥有正确的 POC 流程，并将 POC 视为坦率地说不仅是试图看看你的产品是否真正工作并交付价值，而是进行商业试错实验并从中获得乐趣的好机会，并尝试看看你能带来什么价值以及你能占据多大份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the core takeaway here is, for AI companies, you no longer can just grow and figure out monetization later.
zh: 所以这里的核心结论是，对于 AI 公司，你不再能只是先增长然后再弄清楚如何变现。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And they try to undo it with having more sophisticated, let's say, products that are actually higher priced or much higher priced, et cetera.

speaker: Unknown
en: That's one way to undo that situation.

speaker: Unknown
